draft.title: Authority in interactive texts
card: In a book or a film, the maker controls what every reader or viewer sees. The maker holds most of the authority over the meaning.
Interactive texts, such as games, social media and websites, respond to the people who use them. Users make choices, post, comment and share, and these actions change what appears.
An algorithm is a set of rules a computer follows. On many platforms, algorithms use what a user has watched or liked to decide what to show next, so two users may see different feeds.
So control over meaning is shared. The maker sets up the space and its rules, while users and algorithms help shape what is shown and how it is read.
draft.remember: In interactive texts, the maker, the users and the algorithms all help shape what an audience sees.

a.q: Why is authority in a social media feed shared between the maker and the audience?
opts: Users' actions and algorithms help shape what is shown
The maker has no part in what the feed contains
Every user is shown exactly the same posts in order
Users can only read the feed and cannot change it
a.why: A feed responds to what users post, like and share, and algorithms use that to choose what appears. The maker still builds the platform and its rules, so the maker does not lose all control. That is why the authority is shared.
a.clue: Think about who and what decides which posts appear.

b.q: Two students open the same video app. Ravi has watched many cooking videos and Mia has watched many skateboarding videos. Each sees mostly different clips. What best explains this?
opts: An algorithm shaped each feed from the user's viewing
The app's makers chose each clip for each student by hand
Cooking videos and skateboarding videos are made differently
Each student has full control over which clips are shown
b.why: The algorithm uses each student's viewing to decide what to show next, so the feeds differ. The makers wrote the rules but did not pick each clip for each person. The students also do not have full control, because the algorithm shapes the feed too.
b.clue: What do the app's rules do with what a user has watched?

a.best: Users' actions and algorithms help shape what is shown

b.best: An algorithm shaped each feed from the user's viewing
